I've set the 20 experiments up as 10 matched pairs. In each pair the edit is the same, and the two parents differ only on the condition edge, so any gap in the measured effect can be put down to that one edge.

**Pairs (edit | condition tested):**

1. Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 3 is skip_connect vs none (does the residual from input to output change the value of a final conv?)
2. Edge 3 → skip_connect | edge 5 is none vs nor_conv_3x3 (is a residual worth more when the other path into the output is weak?)
3. Edge 0 → none | edge 3 is none vs nor_conv_3x3 (removing edge 0 may leave the cell with too few paths)
4. Edge 1 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 5 is none vs nor_conv_3x3 (node 2's inputs only matter if node 2 reaches the output)
5. Edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 0 is none vs nor_conv_3x3 (does node 1 carry any signal?)
6. Edge 2 → nor_conv_3x3 | the op it replaces is avg_pool_3x3 vs skip_connect (here the condition edge is the edited edge)
7. Edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3 | the op it replaces is skip_connect vs none
8. Edge 5 → avg_pool_3x3 | edge 4 is nor_conv_3x3 vs none (is pooling the last edge harmful only when it's the main path?)
9. Edge 0 → nor_conv_1x1 | edge 2 is none vs nor_conv_3x3
10. Edge 4 → skip_connect | edge 3 is skip_connect vs nor_conv_3x3
